name: Pregnancy Global Kitchen
summary: A week of warm, simple home cooking for pregnancy: oatmeal and firm eggs, salmon and trout, lentil soup, beef and bean chili and a chicken traybake, with a few dishes from Mexico, Italy and Japan. Everything is cooked through and chosen for folate, iron, choline and omega-3 DHA.
howItWorks:
**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's chicken traybake, Wednesday's lentil soup, Thursday's chili and Saturday's enchilada bake each make two portions, so the next day's lunch is done. Cool the extra portion fast, fridge it within 2 hours, eat it within 2 days, and reheat it to 165 F (74 C), steaming hot all the way through. Rinse all fruit and vegetables under running water before you cut or peel them.

**Folate, iron and vitamin C.** Lentils, beans, chickpeas, edamame and spinach carry the folate. The beans, beef, spinach and a little iron-fortified instant oats carry the iron, kept in a moderate range because your prenatal vitamin adds more. Lemon, tomato, orange and peppers share the plate, since vitamin C helps your body take up plant iron.

**Choline, calcium and iodine.** Eggs at breakfast, lunch and snack time bring choline, along with fish, chicken and beans. Milk and yogurt bring calcium and some iodine, and the salt is iodized. Iodine is hard to get from food, so that iodized salt really matters.

**Fish for DHA.** Salmon on Tuesday, trout on Friday and salmon again on Sunday never land back to back, and each is cooked fresh until it flakes and reads 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part. Monday's sandwich uses canned light tuna.

**One size.** This week is written for 1,800 to 2,400 kcal. There is no larger size, because bigger portions would push the iron from food past what is sensible alongside a prenatal vitamin.

recipes.name: Creamy oatmeal with blueberries and walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian bowl of porridge with maple and berries
recipes.about: Rolled oats and a spoonful of iron-fortified instant oats simmered in milk until creamy, topped with blueberries, chopped walnuts and a little maple syrup. It is **plain, warm and easy on a queasy morning**, and the oats bring fibre and iron.

ingredients.note: Plain instant oats with iron on the label, such as Quaker Instant Oatmeal, Original. Iron varies by brand, so do not stack other iron-fortified cereal on the same day

steps: Stir both oats, the milk, a splash of water, cinnamon and a pinch of the iodized salt together in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle bubble over medium heat, then turn it down and cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Rinse the blueberries under cold running water. Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl and top with the blueberries, chopped walnuts and a drizzle of maple syrup.
recipes.tip: Too much for a sleepy stomach? Leave off the walnuts and let the oatmeal cool a little. A ripe banana is a good swap for the blueberries.

recipes.name: Firm scrambled eggs and spinach on toast with an orange
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner breakfast of eggs and toast
recipes.about: Eggs scrambled slowly until fully set, with a handful of wilted spinach, on whole-wheat toast with orange wedges and a glass of milk. It is **simple and filling**, and eggs bring choline, milk brings calcium, and the orange's vitamin C helps your body take up plant iron.
steps: Wash the spinach well and shake it dry. Beat the eggs with the iodized salt and a little pepper, then wash your hands.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Add the spinach and stir for a minute, until it wilts.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently with a spatula. Keep cooking until no liquid egg is left and the eggs are set and fully firm, about 3 minutes.
Toast the bread. Pile the eggs on top and serve with the orange, washed and cut into wedges, and a glass of milk.
recipes.tip: Not up for much? Skip the spinach and just have eggs on toast.

recipes.name: Yogurt bowl with fruit and toasted oats
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian yogurt parfait
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with sliced banana, blueberries and a handful of rolled oats toasted with maple and cinnamon. It is **cool, light and easy to eat** when mornings are queasy, and the yogurt brings calcium and iodine.
steps: Warm a dry small pan over medium heat. Add the oats, sunflower seeds and cinnamon and toast, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the maple syrup for 30 seconds, then tip the oats onto a plate to cool and crisp up.
Rinse the blueberries and slice the banana.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, add the fruit and scatter the crunchy oats on top.
recipes.tip: Toast a double batch of the oats and keep them in a jar for the next breakfast.

recipes.name: Mexican-style tomato eggs with black beans and corn tortillas
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos a la mexicana, with the chili kept mild
recipes.about: Eggs scrambled firm with tomato, onion, wilted spinach and a little chili powder, served with warm corn tortillas, black beans and avocado. It is **a bright, savoury breakfast** with folate and iron from the beans, and the eggs bring choline.
steps: Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Rinse the tomato and dice it. Soften the onion with the chili powder for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it breaks down into a thick, saucy mixture. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Wash your hands after cracking the eggs. Add the beaten eggs and the iodized salt and stir gently. Keep cooking until no liquid egg is left and the eggs are set and fully firm, about 3 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pot and warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 30 seconds a side.
Serve the eggs with the tortillas, beans and the avocado, its skin rinsed before you slice it.
recipes.tip: Want it livelier? Add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the chili powder.

recipes.name: Potato, pepper and spinach hash with firm eggs
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner breakfast hash
recipes.about: Crisp-edged potatoes with sweet red pepper, onion and wilted spinach, topped with eggs cooked until the yolks are set, with a glass of milk. A slow, **weekend diner-style breakfast** with choline from the eggs, calcium from the milk and vitamin C from the pepper.
steps: Wash the potato, pepper and spinach. Cover the diced potato with water in a small pot, bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes, until just tender. Drain well.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Add the potato and cook, turning only now and then, until golden and crisp at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and pepper with the smoked paprika, iodized salt and pepper and cook 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Make two wells in the hash and crack in the eggs, then wash your hands. Break each yolk gently with the tip of a spatula. Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 minutes, until the whites and yolks are fully set and no liquid egg is left. Serve with a glass of milk.
recipes.tip: A set yolk feels firm. If it jiggles, cook it longer.

recipes.name: Lemon-herb chicken traybake with potatoes, chickpeas and broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian Sunday roast chicken, simplified onto one tray
recipes.about: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with potatoes, chickpeas, carrots and broccoli, with lemon, garlic and oregano. It is **one tray and very little washing up**, and the chickpeas add folate and iron. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.

ingredients.note: from a lemon; zest it first

steps: Heat the oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss the potatoes, carrots and chickpeas on a large tray with half the oil, the oregano, iodized salt and pepper. Roast for 15 minutes.
Scrub the lemon under running water, then zest and juice it. Mix the garlic, lemon zest and juice with the remaining oil and rub it over the chicken.

Push the vegetables aside and nestle the chicken in the middle. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken. Roast for 10 minutes, then scatter the washed broccoli florets around it.

Roast 15 to 20 minutes more, until the potatoes are golden and the chicken is cooked through, with no pink left and the juices running clear. A thermometer should read 165 F (74 C) in the thickest part.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Save a pinch of the zest in step 2 and scatter it over the finished tray for a fresh, bright finish. Reheat the leftover tray in a 350 F (180 C) oven or a pan, not the microwave, so the broccoli stays firm.

recipes.name: Maple-mustard salmon with brown rice and broccoli
recipes.about: Salmon fillets baked with a glaze of maple, Dijon and dill, served with nutty brown rice and garlicky lemon broccoli. It is **quick and fresh**, and salmon brings omega-3 DHA, one of the low-mercury fatty fish.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Rinse the rice, then simmer it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, and drain.
Stir the maple syrup, Dijon, dill and half the garlic together. Place the salmon on a lined tray and spoon the glaze on top with a clean spoon. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the salmon is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, steam the broccoli for 5 minutes, until tender but still bright green. Toss with the oil, the rest of the garlic, lemon juice, iodized salt and pepper.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the broccoli.
recipes.tip: Cook extra rice if you like. Cool it quickly, chill it within 2 hours and use it within a day.

recipes.name: Tuscan-style red lentil and spinach soup
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian zuppa di lenticchie, a simple lentil soup
recipes.about: Red lentils simmered with carrot, onion, tomato and a little whole-wheat pasta, then finished with spinach, lemon and a sprinkle of Parmesan. **Lentils bring folate and iron**, and the lemon helps your body use the iron. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot with the oregano until soft, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the lentils, tomatoes, broth and 2 cups (500 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until the pasta and lentils are tender, about 8 more minutes. Stir in the spinach and the iodized salt and cook for 2 minutes, until the spinach is silky.
Finish with the lemon juice and a good grind of pepper. Ladle into bowls and sprinkle with the Parmesan.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: The pasta soaks up broth overnight, so loosen the leftover with a splash of water. Freeze the second portion if you will not eat it tomorrow.

recipes.name: Beef and black bean chili with carrots and peppers
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex chili con carne, with extra beans and vegetables
recipes.about: A hearty chili of lean ground beef and black beans with onion, carrot, red pepper and tomato, spiced with chili powder and cumin. **Beef and beans are a big iron source**, and the tomatoes and pepper bring vitamin C. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the pepper and carrot before you dice them. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until it is browned all the way through with no pink left, about 6 minutes. Ground beef is done at 160 F (71 C). Wash your hands after handling the raw beef.
Add the onion, pepper and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and oregano and stir for a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, beans, iodized salt and 1 cup (250 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the chili is thick and the carrot is tender.
Serve with the toast alongside for scooping.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: For a milder pot, use half the chili powder. Reheat leftover chili to 165 F (74 C), steaming hot all the way through.

recipes.name: Ginger-soy glazed trout with rice, edamame and soy-dressed spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese teriyaki-style fish, glazed with maple and lemon
recipes.about: Trout fillets glazed with ginger, garlic, reduced-sodium soy and maple, served with rice, edamame and a simple soy-dressed spinach. It is **a light Japanese-style dinner** with omega-3 DHA from the trout and folate from the edamame and spinach.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.

Stir the soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, garlic and lemon juice together. Pour a third over the trout and leave a third for the spinach and a third for the pan. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.

Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the trout about 4 minutes a side, until opaque all the way through and flaking easily. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part. Tip the last third of the glaze (from a clean spoon) into the pan for the final minute and let it bubble.

Boil the edamame for 5 minutes, until tender. Lift it out, then drop the spinach into the same water for 1 minute, until wilted. Drain the spinach, squeeze out the water and toss it with the middle third of the glaze.
Serve the trout on the rice with the edamame and spinach, drizzling any glaze left in the pan over the top.
recipes.tip: This works with salmon too. Tuck in a few slices of cucumber on the side for crunch.

recipes.name: Chicken and black bean enchilada bake
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican enchiladas, baked in layers like a casserole
recipes.about: Corn tortillas layered with small pieces of chicken, black beans and spinach under a homemade mild red sauce, baked with a little cheddar until bubbling. A **weekend project** that is made once and eaten twice, with iron and folate from the beans and spinach.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F (190 C). Rinse the pepper before you dice it, and rinse the spinach. Warm the oil in a pan and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Spoon half of this mixture into a bowl. Add the tomatoes and iodized salt to the pan and simmer 10 minutes, until thick. This is your sauce.

Cut the chicken into small pieces, then wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water. Cook the chicken in a second pan, stirring, until white all the way through with no pink left (165 F, 74 C), about 8 minutes. Stir in the reserved mixture, the beans, the washed spinach and the lemon juice and cook until the spinach wilts.

Spread a few spoonfuls of sauce over the bottom of a baking dish. Layer in half the tortillas, half the filling and a third of the remaining sauce. Repeat, then top with the last of the sauce and the cheddar.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 more minutes, until bubbling and 165 F (74 C) in the middle.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds in the microwave so they do not crack when you layer them.

recipes.name: Lemon salmon pasta with broccoli and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian lemon pasta with greens
recipes.about: Whole-wheat pasta tossed with flaked baked salmon, broccoli, spinach, lemon and a little Parmesan. It is **comforting and quick**, and the salmon brings omega-3 DHA while the broccoli and spinach bring folate.

ingredients.note: from a lemon; zest it first

steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Place the salmon on a lined tray, brush with a little of the oil and season with a pinch of the iodized salt. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until it is opaque all the way through and flakes easily. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.
Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling water until tender, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save a cup of the pasta water, then drain.

In the empty pot, warm the rest of the oil with the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the spinach and stir until wilted, then add the pasta, broccoli, the zest and juice of the scrubbed lemon and a splash of the pasta water.
Flake the salmon into big pieces and fold it in gently. Season with pepper and the rest of the salt.
Serve with the Parmesan on top.
recipes.tip: Want it creamier? Stir in an extra splash of the pasta water and a little more Parmesan.

recipes.name: Light tuna and chickpea sandwich with avocado
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic Canadian tuna salad sandwich
recipes.about: Canned light tuna mashed with chickpeas, yogurt, onion, lemon and Dijon open-faced on whole-wheat toast with avocado, with a spinach salad on the side. A quick **no-cook lunch** with some omega-3 from the tuna and fibre from the chickpeas. Light tuna is the low-mercury kind.
steps: Mash the chickpeas with a fork in a bowl until mostly broken down.
Stir in the tuna, yogurt, onion, lemon juice and Dijon. Taste and add pepper.
Toast the bread. Rinse the avocado skin before you cut it. Spread the toast with the mashed avocado and pile on the tuna salad for an open-faced sandwich.
Toss the spinach with a squeeze of the lemon and serve it alongside with the carrot sticks as a quick salad. Keep the filling chilled until you eat it, and refrigerate any extra within 2 hours.
recipes.tip: Choose canned light tuna. Skip the albacore (white) tuna here: it is higher in mercury. If you pack it, keep it cold with an ice pack and eat it within 4 hours.

recipes.name: Greek-style chickpea and cucumber bowl with lemon yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Greek-style chickpea salad with tzatziki
recipes.about: Chickpeas tossed with cucumber, tomato and onion, spooned over a garlicky lemon yogurt with toasted whole-wheat bread alongside. A **fresh, crunchy lunch** that is rich in fibre, folate and iron.
steps: Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of the iodized salt.
Rinse the tomato. Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato and onion with the oil, the rest of the lemon juice, the oregano and a little more salt.
Spread the yogurt in a bowl, spoon the chickpea salad on top. Toast the bread and serve it alongside.
recipes.tip: Toast the bread and rub it with half a cut garlic clove for extra flavour.

recipes.name: Egg salad sandwich with cucumber
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the Canadian egg salad sandwich
recipes.about: Hard-boiled eggs, cooked until the yolks are fully set, mashed with yogurt and Dijon, on whole-wheat bread with cucumber. A **cool, comforting lunch** that is rich in choline.
steps: Place the eggs in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let them sit for 12 minutes, until the whites and yolks are completely firm.
Cool the eggs in cold water, then peel and chop them.
Stir the eggs with the yogurt, Dijon, onion, lemon juice, iodized salt and pepper.
Pile onto the bread with the cucumber and close the sandwich. Eat it soon and keep any extra chilled.
recipes.tip: Make it fresh and don't keep it more than 2 days. Boil an extra egg or two for snacks and keep them in the fridge in their shells.

recipes.name: Banana with peanut butter
recipes.about: A ripe banana sliced and spread with smooth peanut butter. A **soft, filling snack** with potassium and a little protein.
steps: Peel and slice the banana.
Serve with the peanut butter for dipping or spreading.

recipes.name: Orange segments and sunflower seeds
recipes.about: Juicy orange segments with a handful of sunflower seeds. A **bright, easy snack** with vitamin C and some vitamin E and magnesium from the seeds.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and break it into segments.
Serve with the sunflower seeds.

recipes.name: Blueberry-ginger yogurt
recipes.about: Thick yogurt with fresh blueberries, a little grated fresh ginger and a drizzle of maple syrup. **Cool and soothing**, with calcium and iodine from the yogurt.
steps: Rinse the blueberries.
Stir the ginger into the yogurt and spoon into a bowl. Top with the blueberries and drizzle with maple syrup.

recipes.name: Crispy cumin chickpeas
recipes.about: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy with cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt. A **crunchy, salty snack** with fibre, folate and iron.

ingredients.note: rinsed, drained and patted very dry

steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Pat the chickpeas very dry so they crisp.
Toss them with the oil, cumin, paprika and iodized salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and golden. They crisp further as they cool.

recipes.name: No-bake peanut butter oat bites
recipes.about: Iron-fortified instant oats stirred with peanut butter, chopped walnuts and a little maple syrup and rolled into bites. A **sweet little snack** with fibre and some iron from the oats.

ingredients.note: Plain instant oats with iron on the label, such as Quaker Instant Oatmeal, Original. Iron varies by brand, so do not stack other iron-fortified cereal on the same day

steps: Stir the oats, peanut butter, walnuts, maple syrup and cinnamon together in a bowl. Add water a teaspoon at a time, usually 2 or 3, until it holds firmly when pressed.
Press into 3 small balls and chill for 10 minutes. Keep leftovers in the fridge.
recipes.tip: Press a few blueberries into the middle of each bite for a juicy surprise.

recipes.name: Maple-roasted walnuts and sunflower seeds
recipes.about: Walnuts and sunflower seeds toasted in a pan with a little maple syrup and cinnamon. A **warm, crunchy snack** with omega-3 from the walnuts and vitamin E and magnesium from the seeds.
steps: Toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Stir in the maple syrup, cinnamon and iodized salt for 30 seconds, until sticky. Tip onto a plate to cool and crisp.

recipes.name: Veggie sticks with lemony yogurt dip
recipes.about: Crunchy carrot, cucumber and red pepper sticks with a cool lemon and garlic yogurt dip. **Crisp and refreshing**, with vitamin C from the pepper and calcium from the yogurt.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, garlic and iodized salt. Serve with the vegetables.

recipes.name: Blueberry-banana yogurt smoothie
recipes.about: A smoothie of milk, banana, blueberries, a handful of spinach and a spoonful of yogurt, blended until smooth. **Cold, sippable and gentle**, with calcium from the milk and yogurt and a little folate from the spinach.
steps: Wash the spinach well.
Blend everything with a few ice cubes until completely smooth, about 1 minute. Drink right away.

recipes.name: Warm edamame with lemon and a pinch of salt
recipes.about: Shelled edamame boiled until tender and sprinkled with a little iodized salt and lemon. A **fun, protein-rich snack** with folate and iron.
steps: Boil the edamame in a small pot of water until tender, about 5 minutes. Drain.
Sprinkle with the iodized salt and a few drops of lemon juice and serve warm.

recipes.name: Egg and tomato toast
recipes.about: A hard-boiled egg, cooked until the yolk is fully set, sliced over whole-wheat toast with juicy tomato. A **warm-and-cool little snack** with choline from the egg.
steps: Place the egg in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Rinse and slice the tomato. Toast the bread, top with the tomato slices and the sliced egg, and season with the iodized salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Egg and avocado toast
recipes.about: Whole-wheat toast with mashed avocado and a hard-boiled egg, cooked until the yolk is fully set. **Creamy and filling**, with choline from the egg and healthy fats from the avocado.
steps: Place the egg in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Rinse the avocado skin before you cut it. Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, iodized salt and a pinch of red pepper flakes.
Toast the bread, spread with the avocado and top with the sliced egg.
